OUR STORY

A Patron who wanted Pune to learn.

Late Archbishop Dr. Philipose Mar Theophilus believed in building schools on firm legal and charitable ground. He registered trusts to promote education and relief work, and the Malankara Orthodox Church Council of Bombay grew from them into a network of schools and junior colleges.

1989He started St. Thomas Public School in Kirkee, Pune, with a pre-school in an unfinished church building.
His wishHe often spoke of seeing Pune become an educational hub.
2007Dr. Mar Theophilus School opened in Pune, the latest school started under the Council.

Pre-Primary

Uniform rules for Pre-Primary students

Pre-Primary
  1. The regular school uniform for students consists of a black track pant with red stripes and a red T-shirt bearing the school emblem.
    This regular uniform must be worn on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday.
    A white vest is compulsory and must be worn by students every day.
    Every student should possess at least two sets of the regular school uniform.
    Students must wear only plain black socks with the regular uniform.
    Black Bata Velcro shoes are mandatory footwear with the regular uniform.
  2. The PT uniform consists of a navy-blue track pant with light blue t-shirt.
    PT uniform to be worn on Tuesday and Thursday.
    Students must wear white socks and white shoes with PT uniform.
  3. Students must wear a grey zip-up hoodie with the school emblem embroidered on it as a part of their school uniform. Non uniform hoodies or shoes will be confiscated on the day they are worn.
  4. On the child's birthday, the child should be in complete school uniform and not in civil dress. The child may bring chocolates to distribute.
  5. Girls with hair longer than ear length must plait it. No pony tails or loose hair will be permitted. All girls must wear a black hair band to keep their hair pulled back.
  6. The School is particular that the boys have regular Summer-cut or Buzz-cut. Mushroom style haircut is not permitted.
  7. Students coming to school for any extra activity should be in school uniform. They should not be on the campus in sandals, slippers/floaters etc.
  8. Parents have to pay careful attention to the cleanliness of their children.

Absence

Secondary Primary Pre-Primary
Show absence policy

Excused Absenteeism

  • Illness of student supported by medical certificate.
  • Death in immediate family.
  • Quarantine.

Unexcused Absenteeism

  • Traffic trouble
  • Missing the Bus
  • Over Sleeping
  • No written excuse
Request for leave can be in the affirmative for genuine reason only like attending competitions outside Pune. Leave cannot be granted for marriages other than very close relatives and not for religious obligations that can be done by elders after school.
In the Event of Absence
  • Bring leave note signed by a parent stating the reason for the absence, the date(s) of the absence(s) and any other pertinent information.
  • It is the student's responsibility to make up any work missed during the absence.
  • Punctuality and regularity of attendance is imperative. Late comers will be sent back home.
  • The school will not be held responsible in the matter of security of this second category of late comers.
  • Excuse for abstaining from any school activity/programme whatsoever will not be considered unless there is a good & sufficient reason for the same.
  • Commuters by authorised bus, if required to stay in school after dispersal time, will have to make prior arrangements for going back home.
  • Attendance is mandatory on Republic Day, Independence Day, Patron's Day and all the Bagless Days. Any absence will invite disciplinary action unless supported by a written explanation submitted in person by the parent before the function.
  • Pupils must be present on the first working day after vacations and also on the last working day before vacations.

Library Rules and Regulations

Our library is a space for reading, learning and exploration. Students are expected to:

  • Maintain silence and discipline at all times.
  • Handle books and reading materials with care.
  • Return borrowed books within the stipulated time.
  • Avoid marking, folding or damaging library materials.
  • Keep the library clean and follow the librarian's instructions.
Let us respect our books, value knowledge and nurture the joy of reading!

Admission & Withdrawal

Show admission & withdrawal rules
  • Parents/guardians must understand that they cannot influence or dictate school policies, and that all decisions regarding admission and retention rest solely with the School Management.
  • Admissions are granted only against available vacancies, and no correspondence regarding admission requests will be entertained.
  • The minimum age for admission to Nursery is three years and Standard I is six years, as on 30th June of the current academic year.
  • At the time of admission, the admission fee, three months' fees, term fee, and caution deposit must be paid in advance.
  • The parent/guardian is responsible for completing all admission formalities and for the payment of fees and the conduct of the child.
  • Admission is considered incomplete until submission of the Transfer (Leaving) Certificate, along with copies of the Birth Certificate, Aadhaar Card, and Caste Certificate (if applicable).
  • The pupil may be assessed and placed in the class immediately below the one for which admission is sought; the decision of the school authorities shall be final.
  • One month's prior application through an email must be send for the withdrawal. The original caution deposit receipt must be submitted in person to the admin department. Pupils leaving in April are required to pay fees for May.
  • A Leaving Certificate will be issued ten days after the receipt of the withdrawal application, subject to clearance of all dues.
  • A pupil who fails twice in Standard IX will be required to leave the school.

General Instructions for the Parents

Show parent instructions
  • Parents/Guardians are requested to ensure that their child carries healthy breakfast and lunch for school. Bringing junk food is strictly discouraged.
  • Parents/guardians are requested to be very particular in ensuring that their wards return home after school hours, except on days when the child stays back for approved curricular/co-curricular activities. Kindly note that the responsibility of the school authorities ends once school hours are over.
  • Parents should regularly supervise their child's academic work. Any remarks or instructions given by the Principal or teachers should be promptly attended to and corrected.
Parent Entry Pass
  • Guardians must carry and display the School Parent I-Card/Escort Card at the school entrance while collecting their child from the school premises or designated pick-up and drop-off points.
  • Without the escort card, the child will not be handed over.
  • Parents must carry the Parent I-Card/Escort Card during every interaction with school staff.
  • Parents will not be entertained without the escort pass.
  • Parents are expected to follow the prescribed formal dress code while visiting the school for any purpose.
  • The school should be informed about the identity of the person who will be bringing and taking the child from the school every day.
  • Carrying the Parent I-Card/Escort Card is compulsory. Entry will not be allowed without it.
  • Parents/guardians are strictly forbidden to enter the classrooms. All enquiries should be made at the reception. However, parents are not allowed to wait at the reception, corridors, or on the school premises during school hours.
  • In the interest of the safety and security of students, the school gates will remain locked during school hours.

Regarding Payment of Fees

  • The academic fee for the year is divided into four quarterly instalments.
  • All fee payments must be made strictly through the School ERP portal only.
  • No cash, cheque, or direct bank transfer will be accepted.

A late fee of ₹10 per day will be levied in case of delayed payment.
  • Fees may be paid quarterly or annually (one-time payment) through ERP. No other mode or break-up is permitted.
Fees once paid are non-refundable.

Your Co-operation Is Very Essential To

School Policies & Info

Discipline Policy

School Discipline

Discipline

Discipline

Show discipline rules
  • Students must be neatly dressed in the prescribed school uniform. Personal cleanliness and hygiene are compulsory.
  • Nails must be trimmed and clean.
  • Nail polish, fashionable and gold ornaments are not permitted, except small silver earrings.
  • The Principal reserves the right to request the withdrawal of a student if their conduct, behaviour, or influence is found detrimental to the discipline and smooth functioning of the school.
  • Any misconduct, even outside the school premises, may invite strict disciplinary action, including withdrawal from school.
  • Students found guilty of unfair practices or misconduct related to examinations may be expelled or suspended as decided by the Principal.
  • Students must not litter. All waste must be disposed of in the bins provided.
  • Students are responsible for their personal belongings. The school will not be responsible for the loss of books, money, or valuables.
  • Writing on walls, damaging furniture, or causing harm to school property is a serious offence. Any damage must be compensated by the parents.
  • Collection of money for any purpose without the prior permission of the Principal is strictly prohibited.
  • Private tuition by teachers of the school to students of the same school is strictly prohibited.
  • Habitual negligence in school work, dishonesty, use of obscene language, insubordination, or any form of misconduct will invite severe disciplinary action, including expulsion in extreme cases.
  • Students are expected to communicate ONLY IN ENGLISH within the school premises.
  • During school hours, no student is permitted to leave the campus without a valid gate pass.
  • Students leaving classrooms during school hours must carry a valid pass.
  • Games and sports are encouraged and training is provided. However, the school will not be responsible for injuries sustained; only first aid will be administered.
  • No students will be allowed to leave school early except for unavoidable medical reasons.
  • Any behaviour that causes harm to others will be dealt with serious and appropriate action.
  • Students will be issued Yellow or Red Cards for disciplinary violations, depending on the seriousness of the offence.

Prohibited Behaviour

Show prohibited behaviours

The following behaviours are strictly prohibited and will invite disciplinary action:

  • Irregular attendance, unjustified or unexplained absence, habitual late coming, leaving the school premises without permission, and disorderly conduct.
  • Any form of unruly, objectionable, or indecent behaviour.
  • Writing, scratching, engraving graffiti, drawing, splashing paint, or defacing school walls, furniture, or property.
  • Pasting or displaying stickers, posters, or notices of any kind on school property.
  • Use of foul, abusive, or unparliamentary language.
  • Neglect of homework, disobedience, or disrespectful behaviour towards teachers, staff, or classmates.
  • Bringing food items from street vendors.
  • Resorting to unfair means during examinations.
  • Making noise, shouting, jeering, teasing, booing, catcalling, hissing, mocking, or whistling at any time.
  • Participation in any form of bullying or ragging.
  • Remaining in restricted areas such as the playground, empty classrooms, staircases, or behind buildings during class hours without permission.
  • Collection of money, donations, or contributions without prior approval of the Principal.
  • Smoking or use of tobacco products in or around the school premises.

Kindly Note

Important Notice Parents or students must not post misleading, defamatory, or false information about the school, staff, or students on websites or social media platforms. Such actions will be treated as a serious breach of the Code of Conduct and dealt with by the Internal Review Committee.

Prohibited Items

Students are strictly prohibited from bringing the following items to school:

  • Trinkets, jewellery, henna, or tattoos.
  • Objectionable literature or expensive personal belongings.
  • Mobile phones, e-games, pen drives, cameras, music players, or any obscene and objectionable material.
  • Crackers, fireworks, firearms, or any inflammable material.
  • Gifts of any kind for distribution in school, including birthday gifts.
  • Toys, sharp or dangerous objects, tobacco products, alcoholic drinks, chewing gum etc…

Academics

Our Curriculum

Dr. Mar Theophilus School: An Early Glance

Curriculum

The school follows a well-structured curriculum from Pre-Primary to Secondary levels, aligned with the guidelines of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and the syllabus prescribed by the Indian Council of Secondary Education (ICSE). The school prepares students for the ICSE Examination at the secondary level. English is the medium of instruction, with Hindi offered as the second language and Marathi taught from Standards I to X.

Pre-Primary Section

The Pre-Primary programme is designed in accordance with NEP 2020's Foundational Stage, focusing on play-based, activity-oriented, and experiential learning. Emphasis is laid on the development of language skills, early numeracy, motor skills, creativity, social interaction, emotional well-being, and values in a joyful and stress-free learning environment.

Language Skills Early Numeracy Motor Skills Creativity Social Interaction Emotional Well-being Values

Primary to Secondary Section

In line with NEP 2020, the school adopts a holistic, child-centric, and competency-based approach to education, giving equal importance to scholastic and co-scholastic domains. Students actively participate in drama, debate, music, dance, art, sports, SUPW, life skills programmes, and educational field visits.

Drama & Debate Music & Dance Art & Sports SUPW Life Skills Programmes Educational Field Visits

Bagless Days (ICSE & NEP 2020)

As recommended by ICSE and NEP 2020, the school observes Bagless Days, during which students engage in hands-on, experiential, and skill-based activities such as art-integrated learning, vocational exposure, sports, cultural activities, environmental studies, and project work. These days aim to reduce academic load, promote creativity, and foster joyful learning.
The curriculum places strong emphasis on critical thinking, creativity, physical fitness, ethical values, social responsibility, and lifelong learning, ensuring the all-round development of every learner.

Curriculum Examination Rules & Pattern
Academics

Examination Rules & Pattern

Assessment & Promotion

EXAMINATION RULES AND PATTERN

SCHOOL ASSESSMENT, EXAMINATION, AND PROMOTION POLICY

  • The students' annual appraisal will be based on the cumulative achievement level throughout the year.
  • The minimum pass marks in any subject is 33%.
  • Students who fall sick during evaluations are advised to remain at home and produce a medical certificate for the same.
  • Short-day / half-day attendance will not be permitted during the examinations.
33%
Minimum pass marks in any subject
80%
Minimum attendance per term
25%
Minimum attendance, even on medical grounds

Rules for Assessment

  1. 1 Attendance is compulsory for all assessments held during the year. Failure to attend will result in the student being awarded zero marks. Consideration will be given only on genuine medical grounds approved by the Principal.
  2. 2 A minimum attendance of 80% of the total working days in each term is compulsory. Even on medical grounds, attendance below 25% of working days will not be accepted.
  3. 3 Requests for changes in assessment dates or timings will not be entertained.
  4. 4 Students reporting late for assessments will not be given extra time to answer the question papers.

Unfair Means

  • Students found using unfair means during assessments will be awarded zero in that subject.
  • Parents and the concerned student will be called for a dialogue with school authorities.
  • Repetition of such action may result in the issue of a Transfer Certificate without notice.

Examinations and Results

  • On Annual Report Card Distribution Day, parents who are unavailable may send an authorised representative with a letter to collect the report card.
  • Report cards will not be issued in case of non-payment of fees.
  • Answer scripts (except III Term Examination) will be shown to parents on Open Day but will not be given to take home.

Progress, Marks, and Promotion

  • Passing in English is mandatory for promotion.
  • Promotion is based on the overall marks obtained during the academic year.
  • A minimum of 33% aggregate marks in each subject is required for promotion.
  • Students failing in one or more subjects in Classes V and VIII must appear for a retest.
  • Failure in the retest will result in repetition of the same class.

Class III

Seeds of Change

The year began with Seeds of Change, a Class III Green Initiative in which students prepared seed balls to promote afforestation and environmental awareness.

Class X

Mitosis in Motion

Class X students explored the concept of cell division through Mitosis in Motion, using creative materials and models to demonstrate the stages of mitosis.

World Health Day and World Water Day

Special assemblies marking World Health Day and World Water Day highlighted the importance of health, hygiene and water conservation.

Classes III to V

Creative Writing Competition

Literary and creative expression was encouraged through the Creative Writing Competition for Classes III to V, which witnessed enthusiastic participation from 220 students.

World Environment Week

The World Environment Week featured poster-making, speeches, Best Out of Waste, a Deplasticization Drive, a tree plantation drive involving 100 saplings and a cycle rally promoting sustainable transportation.

Palakhi Wari Theme Drawing Competition

Cultural awareness was promoted through the Palakhi Wari Theme Drawing Competition, while students also participated in the ASISC Zonal Literary Events, bringing recognition to the school through their artistic performances.

Building Strong Foundations – FLN Seminar

Teachers attended the Building Strong Foundations – FLN Seminar, focusing on activity-based teaching methodologies and inclusive classroom practices.

Class VII

Mock Gram Panchayat – Voices of the Village

Class VII students experienced democratic learning through Mock Gram Panchayat – Voices of the Village, understanding local self-government and community responsibilities.

Character Closet Activity

Young learners participated in the Character Closet Activity, portraying their favourite storybook characters and developing confidence and communication skills.

Classes III to V

Legacy of the Past

Legacy of the Past for Classes III to V introduced students to renowned rulers and social workers through role plays and presentations, highlighting values of courage, justice and compassion.

Nasha Mukt Vidyalaya Three-Year Action Plan (2026–2029)

The school also actively implemented the Nasha Mukt Vidyalaya Three-Year Action Plan (2026–2029) through awareness sessions, quizzes, pledges and sensitisation programmes, achieving 77% compliance.

Standards I to IX

LogiQids Logical Reasoning Programme

The LogiQids Logical Reasoning Programme continued to strengthen critical thinking and problem-solving skills among students of Standards I to IX.

Class III

Maths Scavenger Hunt

Experiential learning continued through the Maths Scavenger Hunt, where Class III students explored geometrical shapes in their surroundings.

Classes I and II Class III

Best Out of Waste Activity

The Best Out of Waste Activity for Classes I and II encouraged creativity and recycling, while the Junior Chef Fiesta introduced Class III students to fireless cooking, food presentation, teamwork and practical life skills.

ADMISSION PROCEDURE – ACADEMIC YEAR 2027–2028

Admissions open for Nursery, LKG and UKG, subject to availability of seats. Online application form available 16th November 2026 to 24th November 2026.

Dr. Mar Theophilus School welcomes applications from parents seeking a nurturing, stimulating and enriching educational environment for their children. Admissions for the academic year 2027–2028 are open for Nursery, LKG and UKG, subject to the availability of seats. Parents and guardians who wish to enrol their children are requested to complete the online application process within the stipulated dates and follow the instructions given below.

16th November 2026 to 24th November 2026

Age Eligibility Criteria

Minimum age as on 30th June 2027. The age criteria for admission will be strictly followed.

ClassMinimum Age

Parents are requested to ensure that their child meets the prescribed age eligibility criteria before submitting the application.

Online Application Process

Visit the official school website: martheophilusschool.org

Click on the Online Admission Form link.

Complete the application by entering the required student, parent and payment details.

Ensure that all information provided is accurate and complete. Any discrepancy in the details submitted may result in the application being rejected.

Pay the prescribed application fee through the available online payment options.

Upon successful payment, an email containing the link to download the completed application form will be sent to the registered email address. Parents are advised to check their spam or junk folder if the email is not received in their inbox.

Download and print the completed application form.

Attach all the required documents and submit the hard copy in the designated admission drop box at the school gate within the stipulated application period.

Please Note: The application fee and applicable transaction charges will be displayed on the online admission portal.

Documents Required

Parents must submit the following documents along with the printed application form:

Photographs

Recent passport-size photographs of the child and both parents, along with one family photograph.

Birth Certificate

Laminated colour photocopy of the child’s Birth Certificate (applicable for Nursery to Standard I).

Declaration Form

Duly completed and signed Declaration Form available in the school prospectus.

Aadhaar Card

Photocopy of the child’s Aadhaar Card.

Caste Certificate

Photocopy of the child’s Caste Certificate, wherever applicable.

Address Proof (any one)

Self-attested photocopy of residential address proof.

Aadhaar Card Driving Licence Passport Ration Card Electricity Bill Telephone Bill Voter ID Card Bank Passbook

Previous Report Card

Previous school’s Report Card, wherever applicable.

Transfer Certificate

For students seeking admission to Standard II and above, the original Transfer Certificate from the previous school must be submitted after admission is confirmed, as instructed by the school.

Parents are requested to ensure that all documents are clear, legible and properly attached to the application form.

Important Admission Guidelines

Submission of an application form does not guarantee admission.

Admissions are subject to the availability of seats and the approval of the school management.

The prescribed age criteria will be strictly observed.

Admission of siblings is not automatic and cannot be claimed as a matter of right. All applications will be considered in accordance with the school’s admission policy.

The mobile number and email address provided in the application form will be used for all further communication.

Candidates selected for admission to the respective classes will be informed through SMS or email.

Parents are requested not to make enquiries regarding the status of their application during the admission process. The school will communicate the outcome to shortlisted or selected candidates.

The school does not accept any form of donation or gratification in connection with admissions.

No individual other than the Principal is authorised to grant admission on behalf of the school. Parents are advised not to engage with anyone claiming to influence or facilitate the admission process.

The Management reserves the right to accept or reject applications in accordance with the school’s admission policy.

Fees and Refund Policy

  • The prescribed admission fee and other applicable charges will be communicated to parents at the time of admission.
  • Parents are advised to refer to the official fee structure for the academic year 2027–2028 before making any payment.
  • The application/admission fee, once paid, will be governed by the school’s stated refund policy. Any refundable deposits, where applicable, will be subject to the terms communicated in the official fee notice.

The school day begins promptly at 7:40 a.m. The first bell rings at 7:35 a.m., after which students are expected to be in their classrooms. Latecomers will not be admitted.

3. Academic Programme

Pre-Primary (Nursery–UKG)

A play-based, activity-centred programme that nurtures curiosity and foundational skills. The focus is on language, early numeracy, creative expression and social skills, using the thematic framework of the CBSE National Curriculum Framework for Early Childhood Care and Education (NCF-ECCE).

Primary & Secondary (Standards I–X)

The school follows the ICSE curriculum, aligned with the National Education Policy 2020. The programme is structured across three academic terms, with continuous assessment and term examinations. It encourages critical thinking, collaborative learning and project-based work.

4. School Calendar

TermPeriodExamination
First TermJune to SeptemberFirst Term Examination – September
Second TermOctober to DecemberSecond Term Examination – December
Third TermJanuary to MarchAnnual / Board Examination – February–March

Exact dates for examinations, unit tests and school events are communicated through the school almanac and circulars. Parents are requested to plan vacations in accordance with the school calendar and not during examination periods.

5. Bagless Days

In accordance with the National Education Policy 2020, the school observes Bagless Days for experiential, skill-based and project-based learning. On these days, students participate in hands-on activities, workshops and community engagement, promoting creativity, collaboration and life skills beyond the textbook.

6. What Makes Us Different

Dr. Mar Theophilus School offers a distinctive educational experience grounded in NEP 2020 principles and enriched by a range of academic and co-curricular opportunities.

Digital Learning

SMART classrooms equipped with interactive learning resources from Next Education.

Dedicated Educators

A team of highly qualified, dedicated and passionate teachers.

Hands-on Learning

Science and computer laboratories, plus Bagless Days for experiential, skill-based activities.

Critical Thinking

The LogiQids Logical Reasoning Programme for Standards I to IX.

Well-being and Support

A counsellor's room and two infirmaries on campus.

Safety and Security

Locked gates during school hours, a Parent Escort Card system, and the Guardians of Safety initiative with the Damini Marshal from Vishrantwadi Police Station.

Substance-free Campus

Implementation of the Nasha Mukt Vidyalaya Three-Year Action Plan (2026–2029) through awareness sessions, quizzes and pledges.

Sports Training

Training in karate, football, basketball, badminton, table tennis and skating, among others.

Environment and Science

  • Seeds of Change (Class III seed balls for afforestation) and Mitosis in Motion (Class X models of cell division).
  • World Environment Week: poster-making, Best Out of Waste, a deplasticization drive, a tree plantation of 100 saplings and a cycle rally.

Civic and Life Skills

  • Mock Gram Panchayat for Class VII and the Junior Chef Fiesta for Class III.
  • Creative Writing Competition for Classes III to V, with 220 participants.

Performing Arts and Language

  • Tiny Tots on Air: UKG students hosted their first radio programme.
  • Story Parade for LKG and UKG.
  • Lasya 2.0 classical dance competition for Classes I to VI, and one-act plays by Classes VI to IX.

7. School Uniform

Students are expected to wear the prescribed school uniform neatly and correctly from the first day of school. Parents are requested to label all clothing and belongings clearly with the child's name and class, and to pay careful attention to the cleanliness of their children.

Pre-Primary Section (Nursery–UKG)

Regular Uniform

Black track pants with red stripes and a red T-shirt bearing the school emblem, worn on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. A white vest is compulsory every day. Each student should have at least two sets. Only plain black socks and black Bata Velcro shoes are to be worn.

P.T. Uniform

Navy-blue track pants with a light-blue T-shirt, worn on Tuesday and Thursday. White socks and white shoes are to be worn with the P.T. uniform.

Winter Wear

A grey zip-up hoodie with the school emblem embroidered on it is part of the uniform. Non-uniform hoodies or shoes will be confiscated on the day they are worn.

Other Rules

  • On a child's birthday, the child should be in complete school uniform, not civil dress, and may bring chocolates to distribute.
  • Girls with hair longer than ear length must plait it, with no ponytails or loose hair, and wear a black hair band.
  • Boys must have a regular summer-cut or buzz-cut. A mushroom-style haircut is not permitted.
  • Students coming for any extra activity must be in school uniform, not in sandals, slippers or floaters.

Primary and Secondary Sections (Standards I–X)

Boys

White shirt, black shorts and black tie bearing the school emblem. From Standard V onwards, black full-length trousers.

Girls

White shirt, black pinafore and black tie bearing the school emblem. From Standard V onwards, the prescribed black divided skirt.

Socks and Shoes

Plain white socks and the prescribed black school shoes.

P.T. Uniform

Students should have at least two sets of uniform. The house-wise P.T. uniform is worn on the days specified by the school.

Hair

Boys: a summer-cut or buzz-cut is preferred. Girls: hair tied back with hair bands or black ribbons, as prescribed.

Winter Wear

A grey zip-up hoodie with the school emblem embroidered on it is part of the uniform (compulsory for Primary; optional for Secondary). Non-uniform hoodies or shoes will be confiscated on the day they are worn.

School Blazer

The blazer is grey with the school emblem embroidered on it. Parents are requested to embroider the child's name and class on the label inside, so that it can be identified if lost.

  • Primary Standard V: worn during the Second Term, only on Mondays and Wednesdays.
  • Secondary: worn from November to February, only on Mondays and Wednesdays.

Withdrawal

One month's prior application by email is required. The original caution deposit receipt must be submitted in person to the admin department. Pupils leaving in April must pay fees for May. A Leaving Certificate is issued ten days after receipt of the withdrawal application, subject to clearance of all dues.

Additional Admission Guidelines

Parents and guardians cannot influence or dictate school policy; all decisions on admission and retention rest with the School Management. Admission is incomplete until the Transfer (Leaving) Certificate, with copies of the Birth Certificate, Aadhaar Card and Caste Certificate (if applicable), is submitted. A pupil may be assessed and placed in the class immediately below the one applied for. The decision of the school authorities is final.

10. Information for Parents

Attendance and Leave

Excused AbsenceUnexcused Absence
  • Illness supported by a medical certificate
  • Death in the immediate family
  • Quarantine
  • Genuine reasons such as competitions outside Pune
  • Traffic trouble
  • Missing the bus
  • Oversleeping
  • No written excuse

Bring a leave note signed by a parent stating the reason and date(s) of absence. Students must make up any work missed. Punctuality and regular attendance are imperative. Latecomers will be sent back home, and the school is not responsible for their security.

Important — Parent Entry Pass
In the interest of safety, school gates remain locked during school hours. Guardians must carry and display the Parent I-Card / Escort Card at the school entrance when collecting their child, and during every interaction with school staff. Without the escort card, the child will not be handed over and entry will not be allowed. Parents may not enter classrooms. Enquiries are made at the reception, and parents may not wait at the reception, in corridors or on the premises during school hours.

Parent–School Partnership

Education is a shared responsibility. The partnership between the school, parents and students forms the foundation of a supportive and enriching learning community. Your co-operation is essential to:

  • Ensure that your child is regular and punctual in attendance and studies.
  • See that your child is neatly dressed and carries only the necessary books and stationery.
  • Supervise homework and lessons, so they are completed regularly and diligently.
  • Monitor your child's behaviour at home, and inform the Principal or class teacher immediately of any issue.
  • Read school notices and the Almanac, and plan vacations and programmes accordingly.

Meeting the School

Parents who wish to see the Principal need to fix an appointment.

11. Our School

The journey of Dr. Mar Theophilus School has been shaped by the vision, dedication and leadership of people who believed in the transformative power of education.

Our Patron
Late H.G. Dr. Philipose Mar Theophilus

His vision of promoting quality education and nurturing young minds through knowledge, discipline and strong moral values laid the foundation for the institution. His belief in education as a means of empowerment continues to inspire the school's philosophy and its commitment to holistic development.

Our Founder Director
Late Dr. C. J. Samuel

Dr. Samuel played a significant role in turning the vision of the institution into reality. His leadership during the formative years, and his commitment to academic excellence, systematic administration and the overall development of students, built a strong foundation for the school.

Our President
H.G. Geevarghese Mar Coorilos

Metropolitan of the Diocese of Bombay, His Grace serves as President of the school. His guidance and encouragement strengthen the school's pursuit of academic excellence, value-based education and holistic development.

Today, the school continues to move forward with the ideals of its founders, committed to academic excellence, holistic development and value-based education, so that every learner can discover their potential, pursue their aspirations and contribute meaningfully to society.

About Us

Our History

Our Story

History of Dr. Mar Theophilus School

Founded in 2007 under the visionary leadership of the Malankara Orthodox Church Council of Mumbai Trust, Dr. Mar Theophilus School was established with a deep-rooted belief that "Aspirations are Possibilities" and a commitment to excellence in education. Guided by the conviction that every child has the potential to achieve greatness, the school embarked on a journey to provide quality education in an environment that nurtures knowledge, character and holistic development.

Key Milestones
2007
Foundation

School Established

Founded under the visionary leadership of the Malankara Orthodox Church Council of Mumbai Trust, the school embarked on a journey to provide quality education in an environment that nurtures knowledge, character and holistic development.

Award
International Recognition

World Architectural Award

The school's magnificent infrastructure, conceived through the inspiration and dedication of His Grace Geevarghese Mar Coorilos, received international recognition from the World Architectural Association of Asia, earning the school a prestigious award. It was also the only school from India to be included in this distinguished selection, marking a significant milestone in its history.

2016
Affiliation

CISCE Affiliation

A significant milestone in the school's journey was achieved in 2016, when it received affiliation from the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE).

2017–18
Academic Achievement

First ICSE Batch

The first batch of students appeared for the ICSE examination in the academic year 2017–2018, marking an important chapter in the institution's academic progress.

Curriculum & Educators

A Strong Academic Foundation

Since its inception, the school has remained committed to providing a strong academic foundation through a well-structured national curriculum, supported by a team of highly qualified, dedicated and passionate educators. The emphasis has always been on fostering intellectual curiosity, creativity, values and confidence, enabling students to grow into responsible and capable individuals.

Architecture

An Inspiring Learning Environment

The school's distinctive architectural design reflects its vision of creating an inspiring and enriching learning environment. Its magnificent infrastructure, conceived through the inspiration and dedication of His Grace Geevarghese Mar Coorilos, received international recognition from the World Architectural Association of Asia, earning the school a prestigious award.

"Aspirations are Possibilities" — the founding belief that continues to guide every student, educator and decision at Dr. Mar Theophilus School.
— Dr. Mar Theophilus School, Est. 2007

About Us

Vision, Mission & Motto

Our Leadership Legacy

The Visionaries Behind Our Institution

The journey of Dr. Mar Theophilus School has been shaped by the vision, dedication and leadership of individuals who believed in the transformative power of education.

PMT Photo

Our Patron

Late H.G. Dr. Philipose Mar Theophilus

Late His Grace Dr. Philipose Mar Theophilus was a guiding inspiration behind the establishment of Dr. Mar Theophilus School. His vision of promoting quality education and nurturing young minds through knowledge, discipline and strong moral values laid the foundation for the institution. His belief in education as a means of empowerment continues to inspire the school’s philosophy and commitment to holistic development. The school carries forward his vision with the aim of shaping confident, responsible and compassionate individuals.

CJS Photo

Our Founder Director

Late Dr. C. J. Samuel

Late Dr. C. J. Samuel played a significant role in translating the vision of the institution into reality. As the Founder Director, he provided dedicated leadership and guidance during the formative years of the school. His commitment to academic excellence, systematic administration and the overall development of students helped establish a strong foundation for the institution. His contribution remains an integral part of the school’s journey and legacy.

GMC Photo

Our President

H.G. Geevarghese Mar Coorilos

His Grace Geevarghese Mar Coorilos, Metropolitan of the Diocese of Bombay, serves as the President of Dr. Mar Theophilus School. With a deep commitment to education and the development of young minds, His Grace continues to provide guidance and leadership to the institution. His encouragement and vision strengthen the school’s pursuit of academic excellence, value-based education and holistic development, inspiring the school community to uphold its founding ideals.

Today, Dr. Mar Theophilus School continues to move forward with the vision and ideals of its founders. With an unwavering commitment to academic excellence, holistic development and value-based education, the school strives to empower every learner to discover their potential, pursue their aspirations and contribute meaningfully to society.

Rooted in its vision, inspired by its legacy and driven by the possibilities of tomorrow, Dr. Mar Theophilus School continues its journey towards excellence.

Vision

Our Vision

To establish Dr. Mar Theophilus School as a Centre of Excellence in the field of education, with standards comparable to the best nationally, and to equip students with the knowledge, skills and values necessary to become confident, responsible, talented and well-rounded individuals and lifelong learners.

Mission

Our Mission

  • To provide a safe, intellectually stimulating and challenging learning environment that unlocks every student’s potential and instils determination, self-confidence and a passion for lifelong learning.

  • We strive to make learning meaningful and engaging through innovative teaching practices, advanced educational resources, and a balanced blend of curricular and co-curricular activities.

  • We are committed to nurturing responsible individuals who uphold the principles of secularism, respect cultural diversity, care for the environment, understand human rights and embrace their social responsibilities. Through value-based education, we aim to develop individuals who contribute positively to the school, community, nation and the world.

Our Motto

KNOWLEDGE IS WEALTH

We believe that knowledge is the greatest asset an individual can possess. Through quality education, guidance and opportunities, we strive to mould our students into knowledgeable, resourceful and responsible citizens who can confidently contribute to society.

Principal’s Message

From the desk of

The Principal

Dr. Mar Theophilus School
Dhanori, Pune

“Knowledge is power. Information is liberating. Education is the premise of progress, in every society, in every family.”
— Kofi Annan

At Dr. Mar Theophilus School, we believe that education is not merely the acquisition of knowledge but the art of nurturing minds, shaping character, and empowering young individuals to become responsible citizens and compassionate human beings.

Guided by our vision, “Empowering excellence, nurturing lifelong learners. Shaping confident, responsible, and complete individuals for a brighter tomorrow,” we strive to create an educational environment where every child is encouraged to discover their potential, embrace challenges, and pursue excellence with confidence and purpose.

Our mission is rooted in providing a safe, inclusive, and intellectually stimulating atmosphere where curiosity flourishes and learning becomes a lifelong journey. Through innovative teaching methodologies, meaningful experiences, and holistic activities, we endeavour to develop critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, communication, and other essential 21st-century skills. We are equally committed to nurturing strong moral values, secular outlook, cultural appreciation, environmental consciousness, and respect for human rights, preparing our students to contribute meaningfully to national progress and global well-being.

We recognise that every child is unique, with individual talents, aspirations, and possibilities. Our dedicated teachers work tirelessly to ensure that academic excellence goes hand in hand with emotional, social, physical, and ethical development.

We also believe that education is a shared responsibility. The partnership between the school, parents, and students forms the foundation of a supportive and enriching learning community. Together, we can inspire our children to dream boldly, act responsibly, and persevere through every challenge.

As we continue our journey of excellence, we remain committed to empowering every learner to rise above limitations, shine through their abilities, and make a positive difference in the world.

Let us work together to shape not just successful students, but enlightened minds, compassionate hearts, and responsible citizens of tomorrow.

Warm regards,

The Principal

Dr. Mar Theophilus School, Dhanori, Pune

Our Campus & Infrastructure

Our Campus & Infrastructure

Spread across a sprawling seven-acre campus, Dr. Mar Theophilus School offers a spacious, green and stimulating environment that provides an ideal setting for learning, recreation and the holistic development of every child. The campus features a magnificent five-storey academic building with well-ventilated classrooms, thoughtfully designed learning spaces and modern educational facilities.

The school building is designed to accommodate the diverse academic, administrative, recreational and developmental needs of its students. Each floor houses dedicated facilities that support effective teaching, practical learning and the overall well-being of the school community.

A Campus That Encourages Learning and Growth

A Campus That Encourages Learning and Growth

The school is equipped with separate toilet facilities for boys and girls on every floor, along with purified drinking water facilities. Every classroom is supported by electronic learning resources provided by Next Education, enriching classroom instruction through technology-enabled teaching and learning.

Separate Toilet Facilities

Dedicated facilities for boys and girls maintained on every floor of the building.

Purified Drinking Water

Clean, purified drinking water facilities available throughout the campus for all students and staff.

Electronic Learning Resources

All classrooms are supported by Next Education's technology-enabled teaching and learning resources.

Five-Storey Academic Building

Each floor houses dedicated spaces supporting teaching, practical learning and student well-being.

Sports and Outdoor Activities

Sports and Outdoor Activities

A significant highlight of the campus is its expansive two-acre playground, which provides ample space for outdoor sports and physical activities. The playground features a basketball court and facilities for games such as football, cricket and badminton. Dedicated play areas for younger children further ensure age-appropriate opportunities for physical activity and recreation.

The school also features an open auditorium and a multipurpose hall with seating capacity for approximately 350 people, providing excellent venues for assemblies, cultural programmes, celebrations, seminars and other school events. A spacious lobby adds to the campus's multipurpose facilities.

Basketball Court

A dedicated basketball court within the two-acre playground for sports practice and competitions.

Football, Cricket & Badminton

Facilities for a range of outdoor sports including football, cricket and badminton within the expansive playground.

Children's Play Areas

Dedicated age-appropriate play areas for younger children, ensuring safe and enjoyable recreation.

Open Auditorium & Multipurpose Hall

Seating approximately 350 people — ideal for assemblies, cultural programmes, seminars and school events, with a spacious lobby.

A Green and Sustainable Environment

A Green and Sustainable Environment

Surrounded by lush greenery, fruit-bearing trees, flowering plants and scenic views of the hills, the campus provides a refreshing natural setting for young minds to learn and flourish. The landscaped surroundings create an atmosphere of calmness and offer students an opportunity to appreciate and connect with nature.

The school also has essential infrastructure to support uninterrupted campus operations, including generator backup, borewell water facilities and solar power generation. These provisions contribute towards maintaining a comfortable, reliable and sustainable learning environment.

Greenery & Natural Surroundings

Lush greenery, fruit-bearing trees, flowering plants and scenic hill views create a calming natural environment.

Generator Backup

Generator backup ensures uninterrupted campus operations, keeping classrooms and facilities running at all times.

Borewell Water Facilities

Borewell water facilities ensure a reliable water supply to support the entire campus community.

Solar Power Generation

Solar power generation reflects the school's commitment to sustainability and a greener learning environment.

At Dr. Mar Theophilus School, our campus is more than just a collection of buildings and facilities. It is a vibrant learning space where knowledge is nurtured, talents are discovered, friendships are built and young minds are inspired to reach their fullest potential.

About Our Programme

Where Learning Begins with Joy

The early years of childhood are a precious time of discovery, curiosity and growth. At Dr. Mar Theophilus School, Dhanori, Pune, our Pre-Primary Section provides a warm, welcoming and stimulating environment where young children take their first steps into the world of learning.

We believe that every child is unique and learns at their own pace. Through meaningful activities, playful exploration and guided experiences, we encourage children to discover their abilities, express themselves confidently and develop a love for learning.

Our Pre-Primary Section comprises Nursery, Lower Kindergarten (LKG) and Upper Kindergarten (UKG), providing a gradual and enjoyable transition from early childhood experiences to formal schooling.

Stage 1
Nursery
Stage 2
Lower Kindergarten (LKG)
Stage 3
Upper Kindergarten (UKG)

A gradual and enjoyable transition from early childhood experiences to formal schooling.

Our Philosophy

Our Approach to Early Learning

At this foundational stage, learning goes beyond books and worksheets. We focus on making every classroom experience interactive, enjoyable and meaningful.

Our activity-based approach encourages children to learn through observation, exploration, participation and hands-on experiences. Through stories, rhymes, phonics, creative activities, conversations and practical tasks, children begin to understand the world around them while developing essential early learning skills.

We strive to create a positive learning environment where children feel secure, valued and encouraged to ask questions, try new things and learn through experience.

Six Areas of Growth

Learning Through Exploration

Our activities are thoughtfully designed to support the all-round development of every child.

01

Language and Communication

Through storytelling, rhymes, phonics, picture reading and interactive conversations, children develop listening skills, vocabulary, pronunciation and confidence in expressing their thoughts.

02

Early Numeracy and Thinking Skills

Fun activities involving numbers, shapes, patterns, colours, sorting and matching help children develop early mathematical understanding, observation and logical thinking.

03

Creative Expression

Art, craft, colouring, drawing, music and movement provide opportunities for children to express their imagination, explore their creativity and develop fine motor skills.

04

Physical Development

Indoor and outdoor play, movement activities and age-appropriate physical exercises help strengthen coordination, balance, motor skills and confidence.

05

Social and Emotional Development

Group activities, collaborative tasks and classroom interactions encourage children to share, cooperate, communicate and develop friendships. We also nurture values such as kindness, respect, patience and consideration for others.

06

Environmental Awareness and Life Skills

Through theme-based learning and practical experiences, children are encouraged to observe their surroundings, appreciate nature, practise good habits and develop independence in everyday activities.

Experiences That Inspire

Learning Beyond the Classroom

At Dr. Mar Theophilus School, we believe that some of the most memorable lessons come from experiences. Our Pre-Primary students participate in a variety of engaging activities that make learning lively and meaningful. These include:

Hands-on Learning Activities

Children explore concepts through practical tasks and creative experiences.

Art and Craft

Activities such as colouring, pattern-making and craftwork encourage imagination, concentration and creativity.

Food and Cooking Experiences

Activities such as cold cooking introduce children to food, healthy choices, teamwork and the joy of creating something together.

Celebrations and Special Days

Festivals, important occasions and theme-based celebrations help children appreciate traditions, culture and togetherness.

Storytelling and Rhymes

Engaging stories, songs and rhymes nurture language development, listening skills and imagination.

These experiences encourage children to participate enthusiastically, learn together and build happy memories of their early school years.
Our Commitment

A Caring and Supportive Environment

We understand that the transition from home to school is an important milestone in a child's life. Our teachers provide gentle guidance, encouragement and individual attention to help children feel comfortable and confident in their new surroundings.

We place importance on good habits, personal hygiene, discipline, manners, sharing and respect for others. Regular attention to each child's development helps us recognise individual strengths and areas where further encouragement may be needed.

We also value the partnership between parents and teachers, recognising that a supportive home-school relationship plays an important role in a child's early development.

Looking Ahead

Preparing for the Next Step

Our Pre-Primary programme aims to build a strong foundation for the years ahead. As children progress from Nursery to LKG and UKG, they gradually develop the confidence, communication abilities, early literacy and numeracy skills, independence and social readiness needed for primary education.

We aim to ensure that every child moves forward with curiosity, confidence and enthusiasm for new learning experiences.

Every Little Step Matters!

At Dr. Mar Theophilus School, we celebrate every achievement, every new discovery and every moment of growth.

From the first classroom interaction to the joy of completing an activity independently, every experience contributes to a child's journey of learning and development.

We nurture little minds today to inspire bright possibilities tomorrow.

Dr. Mar Theophilus School – Knowledge is Wealth.

Admissions for the academic year 2027–2028 are open for Nursery, LKG and UKG, subject to the availability of seats.

Our Classes

Four Years of Foundation Building

Each class is structured to progressively deepen knowledge and build lasting skills.

Class 1

Age 6 – 7 years

Formal literacy and numeracy begin — reading short texts, writing sentences, counting, and exploring the world through stories and observation.

Class 2

Age 7 – 8 years

Expanding vocabulary, multiplication basics, EVS, and creative writing. Children develop confidence through presentations and group work.

Class 3

Age 8 – 9 years

Introduction to science concepts, geography basics, fractions, and structured paragraph writing. Projects and experiments become a regular feature.

Class 4

Age 9 – 10 years

Deeper subject content, independent research tasks, comprehension and analytical thinking — preparing students for the Middle School transition.

Curriculum

What Students Learn

A broad, balanced curriculum that connects learning to real-life experience.

Language & Literacy

Reading, writing, comprehension, grammar and creative expression in English and Marathi.

Mathematics

Number sense, operations, measurement, geometry and early problem-solving strategies.

Environmental Studies

Discovery-based exploration of nature, community, health and our surroundings.

Science

Observation, experimentation and curiosity-driven learning about the natural world.

Art & Craft

Drawing, painting, collage and three-dimensional projects to develop creativity.

Music

Rhythm, melody, vocal practice and introduction to Indian classical and folk traditions.

Sports & Physical Education

Teamwork, sportsmanship and physical fitness through games and structured PE classes.

Computer Basics

Introduction to computers, typing, digital tools and responsible internet use.

Teaching Approach

How We Teach

Our classrooms are vibrant spaces where every child is seen, heard and challenged to grow.

Activity-based Learning

Concepts are introduced through hands-on tasks, models and experiments — not just textbooks.

Interactive Classrooms

Open questions, discussions and peer-sharing make every session lively and engaging.

Collaborative Learning

Group projects, partner work and team challenges build communication and co-operation.

Creative Projects

Regular art, science and writing projects allow students to express ideas their own way.

Individual Attention

Teachers track each child's progress and tailor support to address specific learning needs.

Holistic Development

Academic, social, emotional and physical growth are nurtured equally throughout the year.

Skills We Build

Beyond the Textbook

Every lesson is designed to develop skills that last a lifetime.

Communication

Speaking clearly, listening actively and expressing ideas confidently in written and oral form.

Critical Thinking

Asking questions, evaluating information and reasoning through problems step by step.

Problem-solving

Approaching challenges creatively and persistently, applying knowledge to new situations.

Social Skills

Empathy, teamwork, respect and the ability to collaborate with peers of diverse backgrounds.

Overview

Where Foundations Become Futures

The High School years are among the most formative in a student's academic journey. At Dr. Mar Theophilus School, Classes 8 to 10 are designed to strengthen subject knowledge, cultivate independent learning habits, and build the confidence students need to excel in board examinations and beyond. Our teachers combine rigorous academic content with individual guidance, ensuring that every student not only meets curriculum expectations but develops the skills, values and self-belief to pursue their chosen future with purpose.

Class 8

Age 13 – 14 years

A bridge year — extending Middle School learning into deeper subject content. Students build analytical skills, begin structured project work and develop stronger study routines.

Class 9

Age 14 – 15 years

Full board-level curriculum begins. Emphasis on concept clarity, practice and time management. Students explore subject specialisations and begin focusing on their examination strategy.

Class 10

Age 15 – 16 years

The board examination year. Intensive revision, mock tests, individual mentoring and career guidance ensure students are confident, prepared and ready for the next stage of their education.

Curriculum

What Students Learn

A comprehensive curriculum that builds deep subject mastery alongside vital life skills.

Mathematics

Advanced algebra, geometry, trigonometry, statistics — logical reasoning and structured problem-solving.

Science

Physics, Chemistry and Biology explored through concept clarity, experiments and practical learning.

Languages

English, Marathi and Hindi — literature, grammar, composition, communication and language proficiency.

Social Science

History, Geography, Civics and Economics — developing awareness of society, the nation and the world.

Computer Education

Digital literacy, programming fundamentals, data handling and responsible technology use.

Life Skills

Critical thinking, time management, decision-making, teamwork and emotional intelligence.

Learning Approach

How We Teach

Our High School classrooms blend academic rigour with practical application and personal support.

Concept-based Learning

Deep understanding over rote memorisation — students learn to apply knowledge, not just recall it.

Interactive Classrooms

Discussions, Q&A, peer teaching and case-based reasoning keep learning active and engaging.

Practical Activities

Lab experiments, research projects and real-world application connect theory to lived experience.

Assessments & Feedback

Regular tests, detailed feedback and progress reviews help students identify strengths and gaps early.

Study Habit Guidance

Teachers coach students on planning, revision strategies and maintaining focus through the academic year.

Individual Attention

One-on-one academic support, mentoring and career guidance tailored to each student's needs.

Academic Preparation

Prepared for Success

Our structured preparation programme gives every student the best possible platform for board examinations and future academic pathways.

Strong Subject Foundations

Classes 8–10 are sequenced to build progressively — each year reinforces and extends the last.

Structured Exam Preparation

Syllabus-mapped study plans, chapter-wise tests and full-length practice papers from Class 9 onwards.

Practice Tests & Assessments

Regular unit tests, periodic exams and mock board papers under timed, exam-like conditions.

Study Planning & Time Management

Guided study timetables, revision schedules and deadline management skills built over three years.

Future Pathway Guidance

Career counselling, stream selection advice and exposure to opportunities beyond school to help students plan ahead with confidence.

Admissions

How to Apply

Five clear steps to secure your child's place in High School.

1

Submit Application

2

Student Interaction

3

Document Verification

Submit original academic records, ID proof and other required documents.

4

Approval & Fee Payment

Admission offer issued; complete fee payment to confirm the seat.

5

Confirmation

Receive your admission confirmation letter and welcome kit.
